add_id_rule: add row j (the 1-based list position) is add-<list name>-NNN, NNN = j with 3 digits; texts unchanged; byte-identical texts with distinct ids are allowed (W1-12)
checks: each edit is written with s1.edit_document, parsed back with the engine's parse_edit, and its add rows are encoded with the engine's edited_corpus under recipe S's max_train_tokens; any refusal writes nothing
codec: P's own tokenizer (manifest data_config.tokenizer, offline cache), as the anchor token audit builds it
combined_rule: for each remove edit given (NAME=PATH:SHA256, a remove edit of P that the engine parses), one combined edit: that file's removed rows plus the list's add rows

family_78b.engine_rule: PP4 (the lead's ruling, 5 Nov 2026): every wrapper kind runs on engine X (engine_x above): untuned_answers, rep_pass, l1_scan and classifier on the pod; l1_score, s3_score, score_edit, add_edit and s_pool on the Mac. Every derived settings file carries engine_x unchanged from the 1B file, and the frozen check_settings refuses another engine identity (R: scripts/stage1/s1common.py:590-592). A run on engine Y needs the settings re-derived for Y (engine_x = Y's identity, a new PINS-78B.json, a new PINS_FILE_SHA256) by a recorded step; none exists. The engine's own jobs (the a0-1101 retrain, a1_pass) follow ruling 10 and addendum A13, not this rule. The kit packs scorer pods with engine X.
family_78b.rule: the 1B file's schema and name, so scripts/stage1's unchanged check_settings accepts it; every value that differs from the 1B file is per family (pins_78b.json) or a documented 7-8B rule; a null is a pin that waits for the event named in waits; scorers_78b.py refuses a command while a pin it needs is null

lists.s4_top.rows.event: the dose fallback (Part 1 section 10): the kept count of the family's untuned-answers pass, from s4_doses_record.json

s3.source: REQ-11's pick: (prompt, PKU-safe response), written as a stage-1 prompt list

s4.source: the family's untuned-answers pass through scorers_78b.py: dose_s4.json (the first 48 kept rows; prompt, untuned answer), Part 1 section 10

name: write_add_edit

outputs.full: --full-out, inside a folder named tmp: add_<list>.json and <NAME>+<list>.json (they hold text)
outputs.record: --out: add_edit_record.json (text-free: per edit its SHA-256, arm, kind and counts; per add id the list id, prompt and target tokens; token accounting)

recipe_use: recipe S's model.max_train_tokens for encode_train (lead decisions L14: read, never hard-coded); 7-8B: the family's main recipe stands in for recipe S (pins_78b shared.untuned_recipe_s = main): PP1 (the lead's ruling, 5 Nov 2026): the untuned-answers pass and the add-edit writer take the family's main recipe as recipe S; the recorded recipe_s hash is the main recipe's; Part 2 states this. make_untuned_answers.py reads recipe S only for model.max_train_tokens and requires REC and S to agree on model.{max_train_tokens, max_prompt_tokens, repo_id, revision} (R: scripts/stage1/make_untuned_answers.py:82-93). S_78 is the family's main config with only the four recipe-S fields changed (R: scripts/scale78b/make_recipe_s78.py:5-10), so its model section equals the main config's, and passing the main config as --recipe-s gives the same max_train_tokens. This lets the untuned-answers pass run before the family's anchor job (addendum A2's order puts the anchor job first; the pass does not need the anchors). Set to 's78' to pin recipe S_78 instead (then the pass waits for S_78).
